messages.subject: Shimmer support for GGIR
parts:
Hi,

I have two questions that are related to the possibility of adding Shimmer support to the GGIR code. This could be by either modifying GGIR to support the existing Shimmer3 output file format or by modifying the file format to best suit GGIR.

Q1:  What information contained within Actigraph file header is actually needed by the algorithm? I presume the sampling rate and start date/time but anything else? It seems as though all parameters are parsed out of the header in g.inspectfile. At the same time, for geneactive, only the "Measurement Frequency" is parsed (or available?).

Q2: If using the existing Shimmer3 CSV file format, as the Shimmer3 can measure from a multitude of sensors, the R code would need to first figure out which are the columns for the accelerometer xyz channels (e.g., by looking at the signal names in the header) and then just load the values in those columns into algorithm - would this be very inefficient?

Below is an example of the existing Shimmer3 CSV file format where the wide-range accel channels are located in columns 5, 6 and 7. The sampling rate could be determined by calculating the difference in the timestamps.

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Shimmer support for GGIR
parts:
Hi Mark,

Good idea to make GGIR also applicable to Shimmer data.

Q1: For Actigraph, only start time, start date, sampling rate, and timestamp format specification from the first line are needed. However, if your data format is constant regarding timezone/country then this procedure could be simplified.
Q2: No problem, this is possible. There is variation between accelerometer brands anyway, so it is easier to add a few lines of code that look for column headers then to try to make all accelerometer brands adhere to one specific format.

In this branch and more specifically this commit I recently implemented similar functionality for Axivity AX3 csv-files. This might provide some inspiration. Note that this specific data format requires resampling of the data, which presumably is not needed for your data.

In this issue Tuomo recommended that a more formal procedure for adding data formats to GGIR would be helpful. I agree, but I have not found the time for that yet (needless to say that I welcome others to work on this).

As I receive multiple help requests per week I have the following approach to helping:
- Once every couple of weeks I try to give quick answers to the questions related to GGIR that have accumulated in the google group and on GitHub.
- For more time consuming  issues or questions unrelated to GGIR I ask people to pay for my time (see also this blog post where I motivate this). For example, the AX3-csv-file reading functionality I mentioned above was made possible thanks to financial compensation by the researcher.
- When it is obvious that an external person does all the work and my role is relatively minor then I do my part for free, or at least I try to if I have the time for it.

Let me know how you want to move forward.

Best regards,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Shimmer support for GGIR
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thank you for your reply - that gives me a really good starting point. 

Interpolation of data could be required for Shimmer3 data. The Shimmer3 can have packet loss during a recording and that is why there is a timestamp added per row of the output files. Other devices seem to use a single start time and then assume no packet loss through-out a recording. Although, maybe that step could be handled outside of GGIR so that the data going into GGIR is 'clean'.

Best regards,
Mark
